basis: Inherited susceptibility to chronic lymphocytic leukemia; haematologic target, but active leukemia or organ damage is not implied.
Thymic epithelial carcinoma; thymus has no listed anatomical axis. This is not lymphoma, immunodeficiency or immune-mediated disease.
Autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; familial predisposition does not change the affected organ.
Babesia infects erythrocytes and causes hemolysis. Hepatomegaly and hemolytic jaundice do not establish hepatic damage; organ failure occurs in <30%.
Complex III metabolic disorder defined by renal tubulopathy and liver failure; encephalopathy is a defining syndromic manifestation.
CNS hypomyelination and neurodegeneration define the disease. Visual impairment is reported in 1/11; motor abnormalities reflect neurologic disease.
Precursor B-cell leukemia of blood and bone marrow; no additional organ damage meeting the frequency threshold is established.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; structural pes cavus and distal muscle atrophy occur in 30-79%. Ocular and hearing damage occur in <30%.
Malignant neoplasm of ovarian granulosa cells, the endocrine compartment of the gonad; no particular metastatic organ meets the threshold.
Skeletal dysplasia with osteolysis defines bone involvement; no supported additional organ involvement.
Inflammatory vasculitis of CNS blood vessels defines neurologic, vascular and immune involvement.
Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neurodegeneration, epilepsy and retinal degeneration with vision loss.
Benign adipose neoplasm arising within the central nervous system; adipose histology does not imply skin involvement.
Spondylometaphyseal skeletal dysplasia affects vertebral and metaphyseal bone development.
Inherited dystonia and spastic paraplegia define neurologic disease; weakness and laryngeal dystonia do not establish muscle or airway damage.
Growth hormone-secreting pituitary endocrine neoplasm; additional organ damage is not established by the supplied phenotype.
Hydrocephalus, GI atresias and renal defects occur in 80-99%; corneal/optic nerve malformations in 80-99%. Cardiac, skeletal and tracheal anomalies omitted at four-axis cap.
Middle-ear effusion defines the disorder; active infection or an immune-mediated mechanism is not required.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder. Neurologic, muscle, hepatic, renal and cardiac injury vary by subtype; no additional axis clearly meets 30% across the umbrella.
Skin aplasia 4/4; developmental delay 15/20 and callosal agenesis 2/4 support neurologic damage. Ocular damage is 1/4 or occasional despite the umbrella syndrome name.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder with characteristic CNS lesions and developmental regression; optic atrophy is not established in >=30%.
Severe factor VIII deficiency; recurrent joint hemorrhage occurs in 30-79% and directly injures joints. Established joint destruction is annotated less often (5-29%).
Premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures is a skull bone disorder; neurologic damage is not inherent to the nonsyndromic diagnosis.
HHV8-associated Kaposi sarcoma arising in the colon or rectum; endothelial histology alone does not establish cardiovascular organ involvement.
Vertebral and limb skeletal defects, congenital cardiac anomalies and renal malformations define the syndrome.
